scope: Historical dynamic Agent B only; no new model evaluation

methodology.task_equal: Mean over tasks of pass/planned trials. Bounds count unknown+missing as failure/success; bounds are not confidence intervals.
methodology.known_only: Diagnostic only; excludes unknown/missing within each task, omitting tasks with no known trial. Never substitute for release bounds.
methodology.failed_checks: Multi-label counts on fail trials only; labels overlap and are not root-cause taxonomy. Unknown trials excluded.
methodology.safety: Five historical flags; all recorded statuses retained. Denominators separately show complete evidence and known trials. Zero observations do not prove zero risk.
methodology.optimization: Recorded trials include failed and infrastructure trials; known-pass/fail subset also supplied. Prices come from historical manifests; latency scope is CaseRuntime plus Billing HTTP, excluding production ingress and real human waiting.
methodology.comparability: Development task objects must match exactly except dataset and have equal planned repeat counts. Model, workers, grader source and other configuration differences remain explicit; this is exploratory historical evidence, not a controlled causal experiment.
methodology.tools: reads measures investigation reads; it is not a count of every tool invocation.
methodology.latest_v5_4: No post-fix live run is included; these comparisons predate v5.4.

exposed_sealed_history.status: exposed historical measurement; not a current hidden release gate
exposed_sealed_history.verification: Copied B aggregates; task equality and raw records not independently inspected

latency_s.scope: CaseRuntime + Billing HTTP; excludes the production API ingress
CaseRuntime + Billing HTTP; excludes the production API ingress

uniform_grader_verification.scope: Only common B trials in the four development runs; no sealed artifacts or model calls.
uniform_grader_verification.method: Validate recorded artifact SHA256, then recompute outcome/behaviour checks, safety and status in memory; preserve recorded runtime failure classes.
